canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across papers, the dominant framing is producing a concise, coherent, shorter version of a longer source text or document. Most definitions add that the output should preserve the main idea, salient content, core meaning, or essence of the source, and some explicitly allow either extractive or abstractive summaries. A smaller line makes the success criteria more explicit, judging summaries for coverage, accuracy, coherence, overall quality, faithfulness, or factuality, and a few papers broaden the task to titles or bullet-pointed key information.

Variants. Most work studies standard document-to-summary settings, but papers also distinguish dialogue summarization, multi-document or long-document summarization, and query-based meeting summarization. The domains mentioned include news articles, Reddit posts, government reports, academic papers, manuals or agreements, and scientific or medical texts, with multilingual settings also appearing and some tasks asking for one-sentence summaries. Smaller variants treat the behavior as document description, text abbreviation, spotlight generation, paper reading, sensor-data summary, or condensing a multi-agent conversation into a final image description.

Space of elicitation and scores. Papers measure this behavior with 25 instruments. The most recurrent are CNN/DailyMail, XSum, LongBench, Reddit TL;DR, and SAMSum, spanning document summarization, long-context benchmarks, post summarization, and dialogue summarization. Smaller lines use many other datasets and benchmarks, and some papers score outputs with human or model-based judgments, including coverage, accuracy, coherence, overall quality, faithfulness, and win rate against reference summaries.

What it is taken as evidence of. Papers link this behavior to 11 constructs, but they do not converge on a single construct that it reflects. The prevailing construct-level framing is long-context understanding: papers use summarization to measure it, and other papers report it to correlate with it, relate it to it, or claim a causal relationship from long-context understanding to summarization. Smaller lines use summarization to measure generalization, language modeling ability, or length generalization, while treating it as related to faithfulness, prompt understanding, instruction following ability, in-context learning, tool use ability, verbosity, or adaptability.

characterization_sections.label: Space of definitions.
characterization_sections.text: Across papers, the dominant framing is producing a concise, coherent, shorter version of a longer source text or document. Most definitions add that the output should preserve the main idea, salient content, core meaning, or essence of the source, and some explicitly allow either extractive or abstractive summaries. A smaller line makes the success criteria more explicit, judging summaries for coverage, accuracy, coherence, overall quality, faithfulness, or factuality, and a few papers broaden the task to titles or bullet-pointed key information.

characterization_sections.label: Variants.
characterization_sections.text: Most work studies standard document-to-summary settings, but papers also distinguish dialogue summarization, multi-document or long-document summarization, and query-based meeting summarization. The domains mentioned include news articles, Reddit posts, government reports, academic papers, manuals or agreements, and scientific or medical texts, with multilingual settings also appearing and some tasks asking for one-sentence summaries. Smaller variants treat the behavior as document description, text abbreviation, spotlight generation, paper reading, sensor-data summary, or condensing a multi-agent conversation into a final image description.

characterization_sections.label: Space of elicitation and scores.
characterization_sections.text: Papers measure this behavior with 25 instruments. The most recurrent are CNN/DailyMail, XSum, LongBench, Reddit TL;DR, and SAMSum, spanning document summarization, long-context benchmarks, post summarization, and dialogue summarization. Smaller lines use many other datasets and benchmarks, and some papers score outputs with human or model-based judgments, including coverage, accuracy, coherence, overall quality, faithfulness, and win rate against reference summaries.

characterization_sections.label: What it is taken as evidence of.
characterization_sections.text: Papers link this behavior to 11 constructs, but they do not converge on a single construct that it reflects. The prevailing construct-level framing is long-context understanding: papers use summarization to measure it, and other papers report it to correlate with it, relate it to it, or claim a causal relationship from long-context understanding to summarization. Smaller lines use summarization to measure generalization, language modeling ability, or length generalization, while treating it as related to faithfulness, prompt understanding, instruction following ability, in-context learning, tool use ability, verbosity, or adaptability.
